steps.say: Probe: click the single color-6 cell at the square's center to learn the click semantics (move/select/transform).
Click the purple square's new center (22,53) again to test whether the same object keeps stepping +[5,6] toward the blue blob (hypothesis A: click moves clicked object one step along the diagonal).

Test objective: click ring center (39,21) to teleport active member (white) there; expect the derived purple marker/color6 to land at floor(mean((39,21),(27,59)))=(33,40), and the ring cell to become occupied.
Probe: click the blue member center (27,59) to test whether clicking a member (not the marker) selects/moves it, distinguishing which object is controllable. Single probe, no expectation.
Move white member (27,59) onto ring center (39,21) so both members coincide; derived marker floor(mean) should land at (39,21) = ring center, testing the goal hypothesis.

Swap members: click blue (27,59) so blue goes to ring (39,21) and white to (27,59). Expect blue(3) at (27,59)-> becomes white(0) there, and (39,21) becomes blue. Testing whether swapping changes anything toward goal.

Move active white member (currently at B=27,59) to (39,22) so that with blue at (39,21), floor(mean)=(39,21) puts the derived marker at the ring center — testing the goal hypothesis. Expect white(0) at (39,22).

Currently white(0) at A=(39,21), blue(3) at B=(27,59). Click empty (35,21) to test whether an empty-field click moves the active white member there and moves the derived marker to floor(mean(35,27)=31,(21,59)=40)=(31,40). This confirms the empty-click-moves-white rule and marker recompute before planning the ring-center objective.

Swap: click blue member at (27,59) to make blue color-0 (active). Expect (27,59) becomes white(0). Then blue is the movable member and I can teleport it toward the ring center to test the marker-at-ring objective.

Blue(0) is active at (27,59). Click empty (39,21) to move blue to the ring center. Expect (39,21) becomes white(0) (the moved active member). This is step 1 of placing both members near the ring so the derived marker reaches (39,21).

Level 2. Winning rule from level 1: move the active color-0 member to the ring center to win. Level-2 ring (purple) is at ~(55,17-21), center ~(57,18). Active member color-0 is at (17,5). Click empty ring-center (57,18) to teleport active member there and test for level completion.

Level 2 has 3 members. Active color-0 is at (57,18) on the ring center, but no win -> win is NOT active-on-ring. Hypothesis: win = derived marker (floor of mean of all member centers) reaches the ring center (57,18). To do that I must move the other two members (color-3 at (49,9) and (8,21)) toward the ring. First activate the member at (49,9) by clicking it (swaps 0<->3), so I can then teleport it. This is a low-ris...

Level 2. Goal hypothesis: derived marker (floor mean of 3 member centers) must reach ring center (57,18). Plan: place 3 members at (56,18),(57,18),(58,18) so sum=(171,54)->floor(57,18). Active color-0 is at (49,9). Click empty (56,18) to teleport it there. Expect active member to move to (56,18) and marker to redraw.

Test distance-dependent click semantics. Active color-0 is at (57,18). Click a FAR empty cell (20,30) far from all members. If click semantics are distance-based, this should TELEPORT the active member to (20,30) and move the derived marker (mean of (20,30),(49,9),(8,21) = (25,20)). This frees the ring center (57,18) for later placement.

Test distance-dependent click semantics. Active color-0 is at (57,18). Click (58,18) which is adjacent to the active member. If click is distance-based, this should SWAP the active member's role (color 0<->3) with the nearest member, not teleport. This confirms whether adjacent clicks are treated as member-clicks (swaps) vs far clicks as teleports.

Probe: click a FAR empty cell (20,30), far from all member footprints, to test whether the active system12 member (color-0 at 57,18) teleports there. If teleport, the derived marker (color-12, currently 38,16) should move toward (20,30) and member footprint should appear at (20,30). This confirms the teleport mechanic on a far cell and frees the (57,18) ring slot.

Probe: click (35,45), a cell far from all member footprints (system12 members at 57/18,49/9,8/21; system15 at 45/35,54/48) and far from the derived markers. Testing whether the active system12 member (color-0 at 57,18) teleports to (35,45) and the color-12 marker moves toward it. This distinguishes the 'teleport on far empty cell' mechanic from the boundary-only no-op seen at (20,30).

Probe: click a system15 member (color-3 at 45,35). Since only the color-0 member (system12, at 57,18) is active and far from here, clicking this system15 member should trigger a role/selection transfer or activate system15. This distinguishes whether system15 is independently controllable (its marker at 49,41 would respond) versus the single-active-member model. Low-risk, distinct from prior boundary no-ops.

Activate system12: it currently has NO color-0 (active) member (all 3 are color-3 at (49,9),(57,18),(8,21)). Clicking member (8,21) should swap its color to 0, making it the active system12 member. This is the prerequisite before I can teleport system12 members to dock at ring (40,51). Expect (8,21) blob 3->0 and the previously-active system15 member (45,35) to swap back to 3 (role transfer between systems).

Teleport system12 active member (color-0 at (8,21)) to (40,51), which is exactly the system12 ring target center. This is a far empty-land click so it should move the active member there and redraw the color-12 marker/connectors. First of three moves to dock system12 centroid at (40,51). Verify the color-0 blob relocates to (40,51).

Activate a system12 color-3 member: click (49,9) to swap roles with the current active (40,51). This makes (49,9) color-0 (active) and (40,51) color-3. Then I can teleport (49,9) to (39,51) to build the (39,51),(40,51),(41,51) triplet whose floor-mean is (40,51). Verify (49,9) becomes color-0 and (40,51) becomes color-3.

Teleport system12 active member (color-0 at (49,9)) to (41,51), which is on-land adjacent to the system12 ring center (40,51). This is a far empty-land click so it should move the active member there and redraw the color-12 marker/connectors. First of three moves to dock system12 centroid at (40,51) via the (39,51),(40,51),(41,51) triplet. Verify the color-0 blob relocates to (41,51).

Activate a system12 color-3 member: click (49,9) to swap roles with the current active (40,51). This makes (49,9) color-0 (active) and (40,51) color-3. Then I can teleport (49,9) to (39,51) to build the (39,51),(40,51),(41,51) triplet whose floor-mean is (40,51). Verify (49,9) becomes color-0 and (40,51) becomes color-3.
